rationales: Input is data given to an algorithm, not its starting symbol.
Goto is a control instruction, not the usual starting symbol.
Set assigns a value and does not mark the algorithm's beginning.
Start marks the beginning of an algorithm.
DHCP does not stand for Data Hosting Computer Protocol.
DHCP does not stand for Dynamic Host Computer Protocol.
DHCP stands for Dynamic Host Configuration Protocol.
DHCP does not stand for Dynamic Host Common Protocol.
Routers connect multiple networks together.
Channels are communication paths, not what routers connect together.
Addresses identify devices or destinations rather than networks being connected.
Layers are parts of network models, not what routers connect together.
Hacking is a cybercrime when it involves unauthorized access.
Phishing is a cybercrime that uses deception to obtain information.
Identity theft is a cybercrime involving misuse of someone’s identity.
Decryption is the process of converting encrypted data back to readable form and is not inherently a cybercrime.
An eight-character password is generally a recommended minimum length.
Avoiding a username in a password makes it harder to guess.
Uppercase letters can add complexity to a password.
Using only your name makes a password easy to guess and is not a good characteristic.
Bits are the basic form in which data is stored in computer storage.
A byte is a group of bits rather than the basic binary unit asked for here.
A word is a group of bits processed together by a computer.
A character is represented by a pattern of bits rather than being the basic storage form.
The <title> tag defines the title of an HTML document.

The

tag is used to define a paragraph.
The <hr> tag creates a thematic break or horizontal rule.

The
tag inserts a line break.

The
tag is a singular, or void, HTML tag with no closing tag.

The

tag normally has an opening and a closing tag.
The <body> tag has an opening and a closing tag.
The <head> tag has an opening and a closing tag.
An algorithm is a defined set of steps for solving a problem.
A terminal is a flowchart symbol, not what an algorithm produces.
An output may result from executing an algorithm, but the algorithm itself is defined as a set of steps.
Analysis is part of problem solving and is not the defined set produced by an algorithm.
The terminal symbol represents the start and end of a flowchart.
A connector links parts of a flowchart and does not indicate its start or end.
A process symbol represents an operation or instruction.
A decision symbol represents a condition or branching point.
Problem solving is the process of finding a solution to a difficult or complex problem.
Defining a problem is one stage of solving it, not the whole process.
Using guesses is not the general name for solving complex problems.
Acting it out is one possible technique, not the general process.
Importance does not describe how secondary memory stores data.
Secondary memory is generally less expensive per unit than primary memory.
Temporary storage is characteristic of volatile memory, not secondary memory.
Secondary memory stores data permanently, even when power is off.
In the conventional binary unit system used here, 1024 bytes equal 1 kilobyte.
1024 bytes are not 1 megabyte.
1024 bytes are not 1 terabyte.
1024 bytes are not 1 gigabyte.
A prototype can help identify design problems early and save time during development.
Analysis helps understand a problem but is not the best match for this stated benefit.
A candidate solution is a proposed answer, but the option does not identify the time-saving technique intended here.
Start is a flowchart or algorithm label and does not itself help save time.
The expression shows the distributive law of AND over OR.
The associative law changes grouping without changing the order of terms.
The commutative law changes the order of terms.
Conductive law is not the name of a Boolean algebra law represented by this expression.
